title: Supreme Court Reads Whole Contract to Fix Goa as Arbitration Seat, Sets Aside Delhi HC's Arbitrator Appointment
case_name: Arcis Clean Energy Pvt. Ltd. v. Parshva Innovation
card_summary: The Supreme Court set aside a Delhi High Court order appointing an arbitrator under Section 11(6), in a dispute under a 2023 franchise agreement naming both Delhi and Goa in its arbitration clause. It held the seat cannot be fixed from that clause alone where it names two places; the governing law and jurisdiction clause pointed exclusively to Goa, so Delhi was only a venue and lacked jurisdiction.
card_tip: Draft arbitration clauses that name one place only. Where a clause unavoidably names two, make sure the governing law and jurisdiction clause does not point elsewhere, or expect that clause to decide the seat later.
verification_notes: Decision date (12 October 2026), bench, citation 2026 INSC 1109, the franchise agreement background and the holding that the seat is read from the whole contract (not the arbitration clause alone) are consistent across Verdictum, LawBeat and LiveLaw Biz. Some secondary sources spell the respondent 'Parashva'; this card follows the spelling used in the Verdictum and LawBeat case titles.
